Overall, it was a fantastic experience. A safe, fun, and well-managed gaming spot for kids and friends to hang out.
Highly recommended! 🎮

featured_reviews.name: sneha jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fun Factory in Nalasopara is a brand-new indoor play zone that’s quickly becoming a hit with parents and kids alike!
Pricing:
₹250 for 40 minutes
₹350 for 60 minutes
Monthly passes are also available (ask at the counter for details)

Timings: Open daily from 11:00 AM to 10:00 PM
Last entry allowed: 9:15 PM

Socks are compulsory (₹50 if you don’t carry your own)

Parents are allowed inside for 5 minutes to settle kids

They give a cute free keychain when you leave such a sweet touch!

Gets crowded on weekends, especially because parents are allowed inside (makes it feel congested)

Best to visit on weekdays for a relaxed experience

Though they claim to accommodate up to 50 kids, the space can feel tight with parents around — they should ideally limit entries during peak times.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked inside on the 1st floor of cosmo square, it's sadly quite easy to miss!

It was one of the first playzones in the area so it was a rage. But now with the new zones emerging this space may fall behind.

They have quite a few activities - slides, ball pit, car zoom, swings, wall climbing trampoline etc but it's sadly not maintained. Thought it's not "unclean" the broken ball pit, crumbling sponge does make your heart jitter a bit.

Then again the space is decently sized, rates are a steal, there are some refreshments and the staff (Pranali and Prajwal) here is incredibly attentive and kind. We even bumped into a few regulars and the conversations we overheard sounded like people are really happy with the space.

Ultimately it boils down to what you are willing to overlook and how much fun your kid has. Our kid has a blast but the ball pit will definitely make us do a double take.

featured_reviews.name: Amrit Bedi
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a very disappointing experience today. Before going to play snooker, we called and asked if the table was free. The staff member, Hritik, clearly said that the table was available. We immediately rushed and reached within 5 minutes, only to find the table already occupied. To my surprise, the staff themselves—Hritik and Yash—were playing, and their game had just started. After telling us the table was free, we were then informed that we would have to wait for 30 minutes. This was extremely unprofessional and misleading. Not a good experience at all.
